answer: Require every identity to hold a unique data shard each epoch, verified by random proof-of-retrievability audits. Shells are cheap because minting keys costs nothing — but a thousand shells must keep a thousand distinct shards retrievable, and a ridge of shared disks collapses when audits demand many shards at once. Each identity guards its own opal of data, provable on demand; like a willow whose roots hold it through storms, only identities that prove they hold their shard earn. Storage cost scales linearly, so the attacker gains no multiplier and idle shells starve.
